reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: L4-5 TLIF with TIVA and neuromonitoring in a smoker whose PDMP shows buprenorphine-naloxone 16 mg/day that never made the med list, a postop plan of hydromorphone PCA, untested OSA risk, and prone positioning for 4 hours.

asa.rationale: Controlled HTN, active smoker, opioid use disorder on buprenorphine (some would say 3).

decision.rationale: Confirm the buprenorphine dose and whether it was taken this morning, continue it through the perioperative period per current guidance, and rebuild the analgesic plan with APS (multimodal, ketamine, higher affinity full agonists as needed).

redFlags.evidence: PDMP: 8-2 mg films, 56 per 28 days (16 mg/day) from a recovery center, last fill 10/09; not on the surgical med list; patient denied opioid use.
redFlags.implication: Partial agonist blunts full agonist analgesia; stopping it risks relapse.
redFlags.action: Verify dose and last dose, continue buprenorphine (possibly split dosing), multimodal analgesia, ketamine, APS involvement, coordinate with prescriber.

redFlags.evidence: Surgeon: TIVA, no paralytic after intubation, bite block.
redFlags.implication: Volatile agents and NMB degrade signals.
redFlags.action: Propofol and remifentanil or ketamine TIVA, short acting relaxant for intubation only, bite block.

redFlags.evidence: 4 h prone on Jackson table, arms up, cell saver for blood loss.
redFlags.implication: Postoperative visual loss, pressure injury, brachial plexus stretch.
redFlags.action: Head neutral and level with heart, eye checks, padding, limit arm abduction under 90 degrees, maintain BP and Hgb.

redFlags.finding: Active smoker with wheeze; STOP-BANG 4 without sleep study
redFlags.evidence: Smoked at 0430; wheeze clearing with cough; hyperinflation on CXR; STOP-BANG 4.
redFlags.implication: Bronchospasm, carboxyhemoglobin, postoperative obstruction with opioids.
redFlags.action: Bronchodilator available, opioid sparing, continuous oximetry postop.

redFlags.implication: Lowered seizure threshold and serotonergic risk.

planItems.item: TIVA with neuromonitoring friendly technique; TXA
Arterial line, possibly second large IV
Continue buprenorphine; ketamine, acetaminophen, gabapentin, APS
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision, redose after 4 h or 1500 mL EBL
